class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Multiply new coordinates by P to get standard ones.',
            'P translates from the tilted system back to standard.',
            'Use the inverse of P to go the other way.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Transformation Formula", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW
        BRIDGE_COLOR = "#00FFFF" # Cyan for Bridge
        INVERSE_COLOR = "#FFD700" # Gold

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)

        # Formula: [v]_std = P * [v]_new
        formula_std = MathTex(
            r"[\vec{v}]_{\text{std}} = P \cdot [\vec{v}]_{\text{new}}",
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula_std, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula_std))
        self.wait(1)

        # Concrete matrix multiplication
        # P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]], v_new = [1, 1]
        matrix_p = Matrix([[2, -1], [1, 1]], 
                         left_bracket="[", 
                         right_bracket="]").scale(0.7)
        vector_new = Matrix([[1], [1]], 
                           left_bracket="[", 
                           right_bracket="]").scale(0.7)
        equals_sign = MathTex("=").scale(0.7)
        vector_std = Matrix([[1], [2]], 
                           left_bracket="[", 
                           right_bracket="]").scale(0.7)

        self.place_in_area(mult_group, "C2", "D5", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Create(mult_group))
        self.wait(1)

        std_label = Text("Standard", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(std_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        std_label.next_to(vector_std, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(std_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )

        # Highlight P as the 'Bridge'
        bridge_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_p, color=BRIDGE_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        bridge_label = Text("Bridge", font_size=20, color=BRIDGE_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(bridge_label, "C1", scale_factor=1.0)
        bridge_label.next_to(bridge_rect, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(bridge_rect), Write(bridge_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )

        # Inverse Formula: [v]_new = P^-1 * [v]_std
        formula_inv = MathTex(
            r"[\vec{v}]_{\text{new}} = ", "P^{-1}", r"\cdot [\vec{v}]_{\text{std}}",
            color=WHITE
        )
        # Manually highlight the P^-1 part
        formula_inv[1].set_color(INVERSE_COLOR)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula_inv, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Write(formula_inv))
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup/highlight inverse
        self.play(Indicate(formula_inv[1], color=INVERSE_COLOR, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

The animation sequence is as follows:
1.  **Standard Basis:** We begin by displaying the standard gray coordinate grid with unit vectors $\hat{i}$ (green) and $\hat{j}$ (blue).
2.  **Defining New Basis Vectors:** We introduce the new basis vectors $\vec{b}_1 = [2, 1]^T$ (red) and $\vec{b}_2 = [-1, 1]^T$ (orange).
3.  **Tilted Grid Transformation:** The standard grid transforms into a "tilted" red grid where each cell is a parallelogram defined by the new basis vectors. The original unit vectors fade away as the new coordinate system takes over.
4.  **Coordinates in the New System:** We identify a point with coordinates $[1, 1]_B$ in the new system. This point corresponds to $1 \cdot \vec{b}_1 + 1 \cdot \vec{b}_2$.
5.  **Linear Combination Path:** We visualize how to reach this point by following $\vec{b}_1$ and then $\vec{b}_2$, emphasizing that the "address" of a point changes when we change our perspective (basis).
